comparison.objective: PR-1520 joins furniture panels by orienting two eccentric cams, aligning and inserting a shelf over bolts/dowels, then locking the joint. The candidate calibrates and locks a robot-gripper opening stop, then verifies retained motion.
comparison.physical_skill: PR-1520 tests panel alignment/insertion and sequential screwdriver operation of two cams. The candidate tests simultaneous concentric hex-driver and thin-wrench countertorque so jam-nut tightening does not disturb a screw-defined angle, followed by articulated cycling.
comparison.success_condition: PR-1520 requires both bolt heads captured, cams rotated at least 120°, joint gap ≤0.5 mm, tools returned, and hands clear; its body also makes forceful insertion against a closed cam a zero-score damage state. The candidate requires a 90° setting within 3°, retained nuts, ≤2° drift through three cycles, tool withdrawal, and 30 mm clearance for one second. No material rubric detail is missing for this comparison.
comparison.reason: Both involve rotary tools and locking, but PR-1520 primarily tests connector orientation plus panel insertion and eccentric latching, not preserving an adjustable stop under locknut reaction and validating retained mechanism motion.
